implementation_notes: `TrieMap.putIfAbsent(k, v)` returns Option[V]: None means this thread won the claim, Some means the key was already present - a lock-free atomic claim that replaces the classic seen-set on the JVM. It is process-local, so with several JVMs on one queue each claims independently; pair it with a durable store, or with the deduplication offered by reliable-delivery tooling, when duplicates can outlive the process.
pitfalls: TrieMap state is per-JVM: competing instances each claim the same key independently.
Values carry expiry but nothing enforces it; a retention sweep is still required.

variants.name: Functional claim with Cats Effect Ref.modify
variants.implementation_notes: In a referentially transparent stack the seen-set is a Ref: `ref.modify(seen => (seen + key, seen.contains(key)))` returns the claim decision and the updated state in one atomic step, so no lock discipline is written by hand. Strictly it is the same process-local state as the TrieMap variant; true durability comes from composing the Ref with a unique-constraint insert (doobie/skunk) inside the consumer's transaction.
pitfalls: Ref is process-local: Distributed Ref syncs only in-memory between nodes, so it is not a durable claim.
Ref updates are atomic but not transactional with external effects; a crash after the claim can swallow a retry unless the claim is rolled back or reconciled.
